correctness.rationale: The proof establishes both directions of the two-cap equality using range-normalized test functions and explicit sign-saturated star potentials, then proves uniqueness of the decreasing tail-root equation and identifies its closed-form solution on sorted tail intervals. originality.rationale: Primary general LP work (arXiv:2206.12234, Section 6), norming/extremal theory (arXiv:2305.08500), and a quasi-linear tree generalized transport algorithm (arXiv:2006.02703) do not state or directly imply this exact two-tail root and \(O(n\log n)\) scalar algorithm for the sum-normalized Dudley norm on heterogeneous stars. An online result for equal-arm stars is acknowledged as covered; unequal arms with multiple distinct tail intervals are the newly considered case. No equivalent statement was found in targeted scientific searches; residual priority risk remains.

value.rationale: For a natural infinite family of heterogeneous metric stars, the result determines a useful dual measure norm exactly, constructs a maximizing test function, identifies a sharp one/two-cap transition, and replaces a generic finite high-dimensional linear program with \(O(n\log n)\) sorting and scanning. Distinct sign-specific geometric scales are not captured by the equal-arm special case.
